Leave me my children.
JASON
Gods! What are you asking?
MEDEE
Either grace or justice;
At this price, I will forget the evils I have suffered.
JASON
Leave you my children, what a cruel sacrifice!
MEDEE
You'll soon have more expensive ones.
JASON
I'll give them up!
I can't agree to it.
MEDEE
Jason, listen to me!
I demand my sons: you want them for you;
Let their love choose, and be judge among us;
If their innocent hearts, touched by my misery,
Recognize my voice, want to follow their mother,
Ah, don't force this tender movement!
JASON
I cannot consent to their banishment.
MEDEE
Am I unhappy enough? O unheard of rigor!
My sons! My sons!
JASON
No, nothing can separate me from it,
Don't ask, stop hoping.
I would rather give and my blood and my life.
MEDEE
He loves them. It is enough; I will leave them to you.
I will leave without them; far from them I will perish.
You demand my death, I sacrifice it.
O light of the sun! O heavenly righteousness!
JASON
The gods are witnesses to me that my sensitive heart
You refuse this dear favor to regret.
MEDEE
Dear children, I must abandon you!
My sons, I lost you forever!
I will live far from see, your father orders it:
I will die from you; I will not see you any more.
JASON
You will still enjoy their sweet presence!
Until you leave, I'll leave them with you.
MEDEE
Ah, Lord, such a sweet blessing!
Will not be without reward,
What! I will see them again, these fruits of our love;
They'll remind me of these days, this happy day.
JASON
Painful, painful memory dechiant!
MEDEE
O eternal righteousness! O cruel compulsion!
JASON
From my heart I seek to erase it.
MEDEE
You'll pay dearly for the tears I pretend to shed.
JASON
Creon must offer a sacrifice at the altar;
He wants my children to be interested in the gods,
I'm going to pray Heaven for your favor.
MEDEE
You're leaving me, Jason?
JASON
Live, live happy!
MEDEE
Is it possible, cruel, that I may be without you?
JASON
Forget, forget an unhappy husband,
Enjoy a peaceful destiny.
So it is done, O gods, his heart is inflexible.
That I am without you?
JASON
O tears of a mother, O touching memory.
Out of my heart, I want to erase you.
MEDEE
O eternal righteousness, O cruel compulsion!
You'll pay dearly for the tears I pretend to pour!
MEDEE
Make vows for your sons: I will hear them.
Hell will signal my departure from Corinth.
O my dear Neri, what a terrible constraint!
NERIS
Ah, since you are allowed to see your children again,
Be quick to enjoy their kissmen.
MEDEE
I hate them, I'm not their mother anymore,
I don't know more about them than their father's name.
NERIS
Where do you come from for your sons this furious transport?
MEDEE
Stop talking to me, they're hateful to me.
O you, my faithful slave,
Listen to my plans, and second my wishes.
Your heart will be afraid, my revenge is cruel,
But it's no longer an awful enough crime for me.
Come on, you'll take that bright dress,
This rich crown, and all these ornaments,
From the sun my island, magnificent presense;
My sons will offer them to the new lover.
NERIS
Do you think Dircé accepts them from you?
MEDEE
The presenses of the same gods appear wrath;
My rival will be afraid to offend me;
His pride in my gifts will accept the tribute;
I'm glad that at this price I'm leaving him a husband!
NERIS
What, you want to adorn your rival?
MEDEE
Neri, it's for Pluto that I want to adorn her.
These perfidious presenses, this fatal dress
We'll hide poisons that will devour her.
But let's hurry to prepare this wedding dress.
NERIS
What, will you take on these cruel excesses?
MEDEE
Can they match all the evils that have been done to me?
Come on, Neri.
MEDEE
But what sounds... which songs are heard?
CHOICE
Son of Bacchus, descend from Heaven,
The front is adorned with immortal garlands.
NERIS
Creon and your husband at the Temple will surrender.
CHOICE
Sweet Hymen, listen to our wishes!
Hymen, accept our offerings.
MEDEE
Ah, how I love these songs! how they please my heart!
CHOICE
Of the tenderest husbands, come to hasten happiness!
Crown, O sweet Hymen, this happy day.
MEDEE
Listen also to my voice, Hymen, O hymney.
CREON
Listen to my prayer.
DIRCE
And get my sermens.
MEDEE
Bring the wife a brilliant tiara?
What can I offer it and tie it myself!
JASON
Hymen, get my vows, watch over my children.
MEDEE
Singing, wealthy husband, signal your tenderness,
Tartarus applauds your songs of joy.
CHOICE
The front adorned by Myrthes immortals,
Hasten to come down, O hymned heavenly.
MEDEE
I'm coming, too. I'm coming to your altars.
I demand the faith Jason gave me!
CHOICE
The front adorned by Myrthes immortals,
Hasten to come down, O hymned heavenly.
Receiving from two spouses the solemn sermens,
And form their days the wealthy frame!
MEDEE
You received them for me these solemn sermens!
Smile at my vengeance, Hymen, O hymney!
